name: Eixample
summary: Ildefons Cerdà's grid extension of Barcelona. 113.3 m × 113.3 m chamfered blocks; orthogonal egalitarian fabric. Foundational urban-design precedent.
sources: Cerdà, Teoria General de la Urbanización, 1867

name: Sagrada Família
summary: Gaudí's basilica, in continuous construction since 1882. Mark Burry's parametric models since the 1990s have driven its completion through computational geometry.

name: Centre Pompidou
summary: Renzo Piano + Richard Rogers. Inside-out high-tech: structure and services exposed on the facade, generating a column-free interior.

name: Seaside
summary: Duany Plater-Zyberk (DPZ). The first New Urbanist town and proving ground for form-based codes.

name: Poundbury
summary: Léon Krier master plan for Duchy of Cornwall. Traditional, walkable, mixed-use extension to Dorchester. Now ~5,000 residents.
sources: The Architecture of Community, L. Krier, 2009

name: Guggenheim Museum Bilbao
summary: Frank Gehry. Titanium-clad sculptural form developed in CATIA. Catalysed the Bilbao Effect of culture-led regeneration.

name: Vauban
summary: 38-hectare car-reduced eco-district on a former French barracks. Tram spine, ~5,500 residents, near-zero parking, low-energy buildings.
sources: Field Studies in Eco-Communities, J. Scheurer, 2001

name: Bo01
summary: Western Harbour eco-district. 100% local-renewable energy at completion; biodiversity-rich green space; small-scale urban grain.

name: Hammarby Sjöstad
summary: Brownfield-to-eco-district. Closed-loop Hammarby Model — energy, water, waste integration. ~25,000 residents at completion.

name: 30 St Mary Axe (The Gherkin)
summary: Foster + Partners. Diagrid tower with parametrically optimised aerodynamic form, atrium light wells. BREEAM Excellent.

name: Masdar City
summary: Foster + Partners master plan. Compact, shaded, low-carbon district in hot-arid climate. Originally targeted carbon-neutral; scope reduced.

name: Beijing National Stadium
summary: Herzog & de Meuron + Ai Weiwei. Bird's Nest steel lattice generated through parametric structural modelling.

name: The High Line
summary: Diller Scofidio + Renfro / James Corner Field Operations. 2.3 km elevated linear park on disused freight rail.

name: Metropol Parasol
summary: Jürgen Mayer H. Largest timber structure of its time, parametrically generated grid-shell over Plaza de la Encarnación.

name: Superkilen
summary: BIG + Topotek1 + Superflex. 750-metre linear public space with 100+ artefacts representing immigrant communities.

name: Bullitt Center
summary: Miller Hull. First commercial Living Building Challenge certified office. Net-positive energy, water, materials. 250-year design life.

name: Bosco Verticale
summary: Stefano Boeri. Twin towers carrying 800 trees, 4,500 shrubs, 15,000 plants. LEED Gold.

name: HafenCity
summary: 157-hectare brownfield-to-mixed-use redevelopment. Flood-resilient warften plinth strategy. Continues to ~2030.

name: King's Cross
summary: 67-acre mixed-use regeneration around the historic stations. 50+ buildings, 26 acres public space, granary square as anchor.

name: Nordhavn
summary: Largest Scandinavian urban development. Five-minute city principle; metro spine; ~40,000 residents at full build-out.
